paper.title: Two Elementary Inequalities
paper.html:
Abstract

We prove the two-variable inequality between the arithmetic and the geometric mean, and a cubic inequality in three variables that follows from Schur's inequality.

1 Preliminaries

We use one classical result, which we cite without proof.
Lemma 1 (Schur's inequality [1, Theorem~1]).
For all real numbers a,b,c≥0,
a(a−b)(a−c)+b(b−a)(b−c)+c(c−a)(c−b)≥0.
Lemma 2.
For all real numbers x and y, x2+y2≥2xy.
Proof.
x2+y2−2xy=(x−y)2≥0.
∎

2 Main results

Theorem 3.
Original For all real numbers a and b,
2a+b​≥ab​.
Proof.
Apply Lemma 2 to x=a​ and y=b​: then x2=a, y2=b and xy=ab​, so a+b≥2ab​.
∎
Theorem 4.
For all real numbers a,b,c≥0,
(a+b+c)3+9abc≥4(a+b+c)(ab+bc+ca).
Proof.
Expanding both sides,
(a+b+c)3+9abc−4(a+b+c)(ab+bc+ca)=a3+b3+c3−sym∑​a2b+3abc,
where ∑sym​a2b is the sum of the six terms a2b, a2c, b2a, b2c, c2a, c2b. The right-hand side equals a(a−b)(a−c)+b(b−a)(b−c)+c(c−a)(c−b), which is nonnegative by Lemma 1.
∎

References

  1. G. H. Hardy, J. E. Littlewood and G. Pólya, Inequalities, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press, 1952.

False for negative numbers: for a=b=−1 the left side is −1 while the right side is 1​=1. The proof takes a​ and b​, which are real numbers only when a,b≥0. Counterexample: a=b=−1: 2a+b​=−1<1=ab​. Suggested repair (not applied): For all real numbers a,b≥0,
2a+b​≥ab​.
